name: TinyPerson
ability_definition: The ability to see details at a distance.

task_realism.reasoning: Spotting people who cover only a few pixels in long-distance seaside and maritime imagery closely resembles real far-vision work such as lifeguarding, search and rescue, coastal surveillance, and security monitoring. It omits other common far-vision tasks: reading distant signs or plates, judging what a distant object is or is doing, and spotting hazards while driving or flying.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Evaluation is offline on static frames with ground-truth boxes. There is no time pressure, no active scanning or zooming, no chance to change viewpoint, and no temporal context. Weather and lighting conditions are limited, and scenes are concentrated at seaside locations. Real far-vision work is continuous, dynamic and high-stakes, and observers can use motion cues and repeated looks.

construct_coverage.reasoning: It measures one narrow slice of far vision: detecting and localizing a single class (people) at tiny scales. The size-stratified tiny1–tiny3 results usefully track how performance falls off with distance. However, the benchmark does not assess resolving fine detail on a target, such as identity, posture, distress or text. It also excludes other object classes and non-maritime settings, so the broader ability to see details at a distance is only partly covered.

format_match.reasoning: Inputs are real high-resolution photographs of natural scenes, not synthetic or toy data. The output, bounding boxes scored by AP50, corresponds reasonably well to the operational artifact of flagging a person's location. It does not capture descriptive judgments or verbal reports of what is seen at a distance.

transferability_reasoning: TinyPerson directly targets resolving distant targets that span only a few pixels in real imagery, which gives it moderate realism and a good format match for detection-oriented far-vision work such as maritime search and surveillance. Transfer is limited because it covers a single class and mostly seaside scenes, and because static offline evaluation rewards detection rather than discerning fine detail. The result is a mid-range score.

2020.model_or_system: Faster R-CNN-FPN with Scale Match (RSM) COCO pretraining, ResNet-50
2020.metric: AP50-tiny (%) on the TinyPerson test set
2020.human_reference: General working adults with normal or corrected vision whose jobs rely on spotting distant people or objects in wide scenes, such as lifeguards, security or surveillance operators, and drivers. They are assumed to inspect the same images carefully, not under a severe time limit.

2021.human_reference: Relevant workforce that visually searches wide scenes for small, distant people: lifeguards, surveillance/CCTV operators, search-and-rescue spotters, UAV imagery analysts, working from the same high-resolution images.

2023.metric: mAP_tiny (%), meaning AP at IoU 0.5 on the tiny [2,20] px interval under the TinyPerson protocol
2023.human_reference: General adult workforce with normal or corrected vision who do visual search at a distance (e.g., lifeguards, security and surveillance observers, spotters), inspecting the same high-resolution images
